design_detail: Single-site, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial at the NIMH Clinical Research Center, Bethesda, November 2004 to September 2005. 18 inpatients with DSM-IV recurrent major depressive disorder without psychotic features and at least 2 failed adequate antidepressant trials were randomized; after a 2-week drug-free period each was to receive one intravenous infusion of ketamine hydrochloride 0.5 mg/kg and one of saline, 1 week apart, in random order (random-numbers chart), each over 40 minutes by an anaesthesiologist from identical 50-mL syringes. Ratings 60 minutes before and at 40, 80, 110 and 230 minutes and 1, 2, 3 and 7 days after each infusion; primary outcome the 21-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) over these 9 time points (linear mixed model, completer, intent-to-treat and first-period-only analyses). Planned for 22, stopped at 18 after an interim analysis. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00088699 (an umbrella NIMH protocol).
can_establish: Whether, in 18 medication-free inpatients with treatment-resistant recurrent unipolar major depression, one 40-minute intravenous infusion of ketamine 0.5 mg/kg lowered clinician-rated (HDRS) and self-rated (BDI) depression compared with a saline infusion from the first hours to 7 days afterwards, and which short-lived psychotic-type, manic-type and perceptual effects were recorded during the first hours after it.
cannot_establish: Whether the effect is specific rather than driven by unblinding and expectation (saline has none of ketamine's perceptual effects and blinding was not checked); its size free of carryover and early stopping; effects beyond 7 days, after repeated infusions, alongside ongoing antidepressants, or in people with bipolar disorder, psychotic features, recent substance use disorder or a shorter illness; blood levels (not measured); and harms rarer than 17 people treated once can show.

sample.recruitment: Referrals from local inpatient psychiatric units, newspaper advertisements in the Washington, DC, area, the Internet, and local and national physician referrals; all studied as inpatients at the NIMH Clinical Research Center. 42 screened; 24 excluded (11 did not meet the criteria, 13 refused) (Methods › Patient selection, 1st paragraph; Results › Patients, 1st paragraph; Figure 1).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Aged 18 to 65; inpatients with DSM-IV major depressive disorder, recurrent, without psychotic features (SCID-P); HDRS-21 of 18 or more at screening and at the start of each infusion day; failure of at least 2 adequate antidepressant trials (Antidepressant Treatment History Form). Good physical health on history, examination, blood tests, ECG, chest radiograph, urinalysis and toxicology; no comorbid substance abuse or dependence for at least 3 months and a negative urine toxicology screen; not judged a serious suicide risk; comorbid anxiety disorders allowed if not needing current treatment. Excluded: bipolar disorder or a history of antidepressant- or substance-induced hypomania or mania. Final selection by consensus of the investigator team (Methods › Patient selection, 1st and 2nd paragraphs).
sample.demographics: 12 women and 6 men; mean age 46.7 (SD 11.2); length of illness 23.7 (12.5) years; current episode 33.6 (37.4) months; 6.6 (4.7) previous episodes; 5.7 (3.4) lifetime antidepressant trials; 4 had had ECT; 61% a lifetime comorbid anxiety diagnosis, 39% a lifetime diagnosis of any substance abuse or dependence (7 of 18), 28% of alcohol abuse or dependence (5 of 18); all but one had failed an adequate trial in the current episode. Race and ethnicity not reported (Results › Patients, 2nd paragraph; Table, bottom row).
sample.attrition: Of 18 randomized, 17 received ketamine and 14 saline. Four people given ketamine first never received saline because they kept a response for 7 days; one person discontinued for medical reasons after the saline infusion and never received ketamine; so 13 received both (editors' count from the Table rows marked NA) (Results › Patients, 1st paragraph; Figure 1; Table).
sample.selection_effects: A small, chronically and severely ill inpatient sample at a national research unit, willing to stop all psychotropic medication for 2 weeks and to be infused, selected by investigator consensus; 13 of 42 screened refused. Two-thirds were women. The authors note that this refractory, late-course group may not respond like people with less severe or shorter illness (Comment, 5th paragraph).

exposure.measurement: Assigned infusion: ketamine hydrochloride (Abbott Laboratories) or 0.9% saline, in identical 50-mL syringes, given over 40 minutes by infusion pump by an anaesthesiologist in the perianesthesia care unit (Methods › Study design). No blood levels of ketamine or its metabolites were collected (Comment, 4th paragraph).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions: ketamine hydrochloride 0.5 mg/kg intravenously over 40 minutes, once, and saline once, 1 week apart, after a 2-week drug-free period (Methods › Study design). The authors state that the dose was chosen from in vitro NMDA-blockade data, mood effects in healthy volunteers and an earlier pilot study (Comment, 7th paragraph).
exposure.polysubstance: No comorbid substance abuse or dependence for at least 3 months and a negative urine toxicology screen at entry; 7 of 18 had a lifetime diagnosis of substance abuse or dependence and 5 of alcohol abuse or dependence (Table). Tobacco and current alcohol use not reported.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: A 2-week drug-free period before the first infusion, as inpatients; how freedom from psychotropic drugs was verified beyond the screening toxicology is not stated (Abstract › Interventions; Methods › Study design).

comparison.controls: The same participants' saline infusion, an inert placebo with none of ketamine's acute perceptual effects, given 1 week before or after the ketamine infusion.
comparison.matching: Within-person crossover; order assigned with a random-numbers chart. Who generated and held the sequence, and how allocation was concealed, is not described (Methods › Study design). Baseline HDRS before the first infusion was similar by order: 24.4 (SD 6.9) for those given saline first and 24.9 (6.9) for those given ketamine first (Results › Efficacy, 2nd paragraph).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to a randomized within-person comparison; but the second-period baseline is not equivalent: in those given ketamine first, HDRS before the saline infusion was 17.2 (SD 6.9) against 24.9 before ketamine (carryover; Results › Efficacy, 2nd paragraph).

outcomes.instruments: Primary: 21-item HDRS (clinician-rated depression). Secondary: Beck Depression Inventory (BDI, self-rated depression), Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale positive symptoms subscale (BPRS, clinician-rated psychotic-type symptoms), Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS, clinician-rated manic symptoms) and visual analogue scales (self-rated, including depression); single HDRS items as a secondary analysis; adverse effects (how recorded is not described). All rated 60 minutes before and at 40, 80, 110 and 230 minutes and 1, 2, 3 and 7 days after each infusion, so the 40- to 230-minute ratings fall in the hours of acute drug effects and the day 1 to 7 ratings after them (Methods › Outcome measures).
outcomes.validity_norms: Raters (research nurses, a physician and a psychologist) trained together; intraclass correlation 0.81 for the HDRS and 0.91 for the YMRS. Response: a decrease of 50% or more in HDRS from baseline; remission: HDRS of 7 or less (Methods › Outcome measures).
outcomes.operationalization: Antidepressant effect = lower HDRS after ketamine than after saline in a linear mixed model of drug and time over the 9 time points, with simple-effects tests at each time point and Cohen's d at chosen points; response and remission compared at each time point by McNemar tests in completers. Psychotic-type and manic-type effects = BPRS positive and YMRS scores; perceptual effects from the HDRS depersonalization/derealization item and the adverse-effect list (Methods › Statistical analyses).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: Seven outcome measures (HDRS, BDI, BPRS positive, YMRS, visual analogue scales, response, remission), each at up to 9 time points, plus 20 single HDRS items. Bonferroni correction was applied only to the McNemar tests of responders and remitters across time points; none for the simple-effects tests at each time point or for the item analysis (Methods › Statistical analyses).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Described as double-blind, with identical syringes; how raters were kept unaware is not described, and no check of whether patients or raters guessed the infusion is reported. The authors state that the short-lived perceptual disturbances could have affected the blind and biased patient reporting (Comment, 6th paragraph).

analysis.effect_sizes: Completers (13 by the editors' count): drug F(1,203) = 58.24, time F(8,203) = 9.48, drug × time F(8,203) = 4.15, all P < .001; ketamine better than saline from 110 minutes through 7 days; Cohen's d 1.46 (95% CI 0.91 to 2.01) at 24 hours and 0.68 (0.13 to 1.23) at 1 week. Intent-to-treat (18): drug F(1,260) = 34.08, time F(8,257) = 8.92, drug × time F(8,257) = 5.29, all P < .001. First period only (between-subjects, 18): drug F(1,16) = 10.44, P = .005; ketamine lower from 80 minutes through day 7. BDI (completers): drug F(1,200) = 50.57, P < .001, drug × time P = .06. Day-1 response 12 of 17 (71%) after ketamine against 0 of 14 after saline; remission 5 of 17 (29%) against 0; 6 of 17 (35%) kept a response for at least a week. Per-patient day-1 HDRS change: mean −56.2% (SD 20.4) after ketamine and −9.8% (20.1) after saline. Editors' calculation from the Table: in the 13 who had both infusions, −53.4% after ketamine and −11.2% after saline.
analysis.covariates: None; within-person comparisons. Carryover was tested on the baseline scores (drug × order interaction), and a first-period-only analysis was added to address it (Methods › Statistical analyses, 2nd and 4th paragraphs).
analysis.preregistration_detail: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00088699 (printed in the abstract), first submitted 30 July 2004, before enrolment began in November 2004. It is an umbrella NIMH protocol (04-M-0222) with several substudies, 67 enrolled up to 2017. The earliest archived version (23 June 2005) lists no primary outcome measure; reduction from baseline of the HDRS between groups was entered on 19 June 2006 (version 2), after the trial had ended and the article had been accepted; the current record names the MADRS at baseline and day 1. The registry's entry criterion is a MADRS of at least 22 at screening and before phase I, against the article's HDRS of 18 or more. Read from the registry record and its history (versions 1 and 2), not from the article.
analysis.selective_reporting: The trial stopped at 18 of a planned 22 after an interim analysis, with no stopping rule or pre-specification described (Methods › Patient selection, 4th paragraph). Adverse effects are listed without counts or denominators. Visual analogue scale results are given for depression only. Figures 1 to 3 (flow, HDRS/BPRS/YMRS over time, responders and remitters over time) are images whose values were not extracted.
analysis.power: No sample-size calculation is reported; 22 were planned. With 13 completers the interval for the day-7 effect is wide (d 0.13 to 1.23).

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 18 medication-free inpatients (13 with both infusions), HDRS scores were lower after one ketamine infusion than after saline from 110 minutes to day 7 in the completer analysis, with a standardized difference of 1.46 at 24 hours and 0.68 at day 7; self-rated BDI agreed. On day 1, 12 of 17 met response criteria and 5 of 17 remission criteria after ketamine, against none of 14 after saline; 6 of 17 kept a response for at least a week. Only the day-1 responder difference survived Bonferroni correction, and remission did not differ significantly at any point. Ketamine first lowered the baseline before the saline period (carryover). BPRS positive and YMRS scores rose at 40 minutes only, and depersonalization or derealization was worse from 40 to 110 minutes.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract concludes that “robust and rapid antidepressant effects” followed a single dose, with onset within 2 hours and significance for 1 week, without saying that the placebo was saline, that 13 people provided the completer estimates, that remission never differed significantly, or that the trial stopped early. The Comment says no other drug or somatic treatment has been reported to give such a dramatic, rapid and prolonged response, and sets day-1 response here beside week-8 response rates of other antidepressants in other trials (Comment, 1st paragraph). It says the improvement is disconnected from euphoria and psychotomimetic symptoms, although a trend linked larger BPRS rises to larger HDRS improvement (r = −0.46, P = .06), and that onset and course were nearly identical for each subject, although the Table shows day-1 changes from −17% to −90% (Comment, 7th paragraph; Table). The authors do state that limited blinding may have biased patient reporting and that the results may not generalize (Comment, 5th and 6th paragraphs).

timeline.event: Berman et al.: placebo-controlled study in 8 people with major depression, as described in this article: a rapid, short-lived effect, with 4 of 8 reaching a 50% or greater HDRS decrease over 3 days of follow-up (not read).
This trial: 18 inpatients, ketamine 0.5 mg/kg against saline, crossover; HDRS lower from 110 minutes to day 7; day-1 response 12 of 17 against 0 of 14.

Murrough et al.: two-site parallel trial, 72 analysed, the same ketamine dose against midazolam as an active placebo; MADRS 7.95 points lower at 24 hours, response 64% against 28%, no significant difference on MADRS or response at day 7. Dennis S. Charney is an author of both trials.

Daly et al.: esketamine nasal spray added to oral antidepressants, 67 randomized, Janssen-sponsored; MADRS differences of 4.2 to 9.0 points against placebo after 1 week. Jaskaran B. Singh and Husseini K. Manji, authors of this trial, are among its authors as Janssen employees.

replication.where_it_stands: The effect at 24 hours after a single infusion was found again in a larger two-site trial that used an active placebo (Murrough et al., 2013), with one author in common with this trial; that trial found no significant difference at day 7, so the persistence to 1 week seen here against saline is less secure than the effect at 24 hours. The systematic reviews on the Tier A list (Dean et al., 2021; Nikolin et al., 2023) are being read by other readers in this round.

funding.funder: Supported by the Intramural Research Program at the National Institute of Mental Health, National Institutes of Health, and Department of Health and Human Services (Article Information › Funding/Support). The ketamine used was Abbott Laboratories ketamine hydrochloride (Methods › Study design); no industry funding is reported.
funding.declared_conflicts: Not reported: the article information prints correspondence, submission and acceptance dates, author contributions (statistical analysis by Mr Luckenbaugh), funding/support and an acknowledgment of Dennis S. Charney, but no financial disclosure or conflict-of-interest statement.
funding.affiliations_note: All eight authors (Zarate, Singh, Carlson, Brutsche, Ameli, Luckenbaugh, Charney, Manji) were at the Mood and Anxiety Disorders Program, NIMH; Charney is acknowledged as being at Mount Sinai Medical School at publication and is an author of Murrough et al. (2013). Singh and Manji are authors of the esketamine trial of Daly et al. (2018), in which both are listed as Janssen Research & Development employees holding company stock (that article's disclosures); no such link is stated in this 2006 article.

what_would_settle_it: A larger, multi-site parallel-group trial (no crossover carryover) of one or more infusions against an active placebo that mimics ketamine's acute effects, with a pre-registered primary outcome and time point, raters kept apart from infusion-day events, a formal check of what patients and raters guessed, and follow-up of every participant well beyond 1 week.

domains.domain: Randomization process (order of the two infusions)
domains.note: Order assigned with a random-numbers chart; sequence holding and allocation concealment are not described. First-period baselines were similar by order (HDRS 24.4 and 24.9).

Baseline HDRS before the second infusion fell from 24.9 to 17.2 in those given ketamine first (P = .004; drug × order interaction F(1,16) = 5.05, P = .04), with only 1 week between infusions while 6 of 17 kept a response for at least a week. The first-period-only analysis avoids carryover and gave similar results, but rests on 18 people compared between subjects.

Identical syringes and infusion procedure, but saline lacks ketamine's perceptual effects (depersonalization or derealization worse from 40 to 110 minutes), so participants could tell which infusion they had. The 4 people still responding at day 7 were not crossed over, an outcome-driven departure from the protocol that the intent-to-treat mixed model includes.

5 of 18 missed one period: 4 because they were still responding after ketamine, 1 for medical reasons after saline. The completer analysis thus drops 4 ketamine responders (which would understate the effect), while the intent-to-treat model assumes data missing at random, which outcome-driven missingness does not satisfy.

Clinician-rated HDRS and self-rated BDI and visual analogue scales with an inert placebo and obvious acute effects; no check of what patients or raters guessed; the authors themselves say limited blinding may have biased patient reporting.

Registered before enrolment, but the primary outcome was entered in the registry only in June 2006, after the trial ended, and the current record names a different scale (MADRS). The trial stopped at 18 of 22 after an interim analysis with no stated rule. The three analysis sets reported all point the same way.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The randomized within-person design and a large, consistent difference in the first 24 hours make a short-term effect likely, and the authors add a first-period analysis to address carryover. The overall judgment is high because the comparison is with saline in a drug whose acute effects are obvious, blinding was not checked, outcomes are subjective, the trial stopped early after an interim look, and ketamine given first carried over into the saline period; together these can inflate the size of the effect and above all its persistence to day 7. The source can be cited for lower HDRS and BDI scores from about 2 hours to 7 days after one 0.5 mg/kg infusion compared with saline in 18 medication-free inpatients with treatment-resistant unipolar depression, for day-1 response in 12 of 17 against 0 of 14, and for BPRS and YMRS rises limited to the first hour; it cannot be cited for an effect specific beyond expectation, for duration beyond a week, for remission, or for safety.

key_findings.finding: 42 people screened, 18 randomized (24 excluded: 11 did not meet criteria, 13 refused); 17 received ketamine and 14 saline; 4 given ketamine first did not receive saline because they kept a response for 7 days, and 1 discontinued for medical reasons after saline.
key_findings.note: Editors' count from the Table: 13 people received both infusions (rows 1, 3, 9 and 13 have no saline value and row 18 no ketamine value).

key_findings.finding: Sample: 12 women and 6 men, mean age 46.7 (SD 11.2); length of illness 23.7 (12.5) years; current episode 33.6 (37.4) months; 6.6 (4.7) episodes; 5.7 (3.4) lifetime antidepressant trials; 4 had had ECT; 61% lifetime anxiety diagnosis, 39% lifetime substance abuse or dependence, 28% lifetime alcohol abuse or dependence.
key_findings.locator: Results › Patients, 2nd paragraph; Table, bottom row

key_findings.finding: Primary outcome, completers: HDRS drug F(1,203) = 58.24, time F(8,203) = 9.48, drug × time F(8,203) = 4.15 (all P < .001); simple effects showed ketamine better than saline from 110 minutes through 7 days; Cohen's d 1.46 (95% CI 0.91 to 2.01) after 24 hours and 0.68 (0.13 to 1.23) after 1 week.
key_findings.note: The completer analysis covers the 13 who had both infusions (editors' count); the Figure 2 legend gives n = 18 for it (see reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: Intent-to-treat analysis (all available data): drug F(1,260) = 34.08, time F(8,257) = 8.92, drug × time F(8,257) = 5.29 (all P < .001); ketamine better than saline within 110 minutes and through 7 days.

Carryover: baseline HDRS before each infusion showed a drug effect, F(1,16) = 6.25, P = .02, and a drug × order interaction, F(1,16) = 5.05, P = .04, without an order effect, F(1,16) = 1.54, P = .23. Saline first: 24.4 (SD 6.9) before the first and 24.9 (6.8) before the second infusion; ketamine first: 24.9 (6.9) and 17.2 (6.9), P = .004.

First-period data only (between-subjects): drug F(1,16) = 10.44, P = .005; time F(8,126) = 8.25, P < .001; drug × time printed as F(1,126) = 4.66, P < .001; scores lower after ketamine by 80 minutes and through day 7.
key_findings.note: The numerator degrees of freedom of the interaction are misprinted (see reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: Self-ratings, completers: BDI drug F(1,200) = 50.57, P < .001, time F(8,200) = 5.82, P < .001, drug × time F(8,200) = 1.90, P = .06, with ketamine better from 40 minutes through 7 days; visual analogue depression drug F(1,198) = 59.88, P < .001, time F(8,198) = 4.70, P < .001, drug × time F(8,198) = 1.92, P = .058.

Single HDRS items: 7 of 20 had significant time × drug interactions; depressed mood, guilt, work and interests and psychic anxiety improved, depressed mood and guilt from 40 minutes; depersonalization or derealization was worse from 40 to 110 minutes; motor retardation and gastrointestinal symptoms were worse at 40 minutes, motor retardation better at day 1. A further 7 items showed only a drug main effect, those named (suicide, insomnia, general somatic, genital symptoms, hypochondriasis) improving after ketamine; no item differed at baseline.
key_findings.note: Seven items are said to show a drug main effect but only five are named.

key_findings.finding: Response and remission (intent-to-treat): 1 day after infusion 12 of 17 (71%) met response criteria after ketamine against 0 of 14 after saline; remission 5 of 17 (29%) against 0; 6 (35%) kept a response to ketamine for at least 1 week, 2 of them for at least 2 weeks; no one responded at 1 or 7 days after saline. In completers, McNemar tests showed more responders after ketamine on days 1 and 2, but only day 1 remained significant after Bonferroni correction; remitters did not differ significantly at any time point.

Per-patient day-1 HDRS change from baseline: after ketamine mean −56.2% (SD 20.4), ranging from −17% to −90% across the 17; after saline −9.8% (20.1), ranging from −41% to +25% across the 14. Editors' count: 12 of the 17 ketamine values are a fall of 50% or more and none of the saline values; in the 13 who had both infusions the means are −53.4% after ketamine and −11.2% after saline (editors' calculation).
key_findings.locator: Table, columns % Change in HDRS Score (Day 1), Ketamine and Placebo, and bottom row

key_findings.finding: Psychotic-type and manic-type ratings: BPRS positive scores were higher after ketamine only at 40 minutes (drug F(1,200) = 4.23, P = .04; time F(8,200) = 9.31, P < .001; drug × time F(8,200) = 6.89, P < .001); YMRS scores were higher at 40 minutes only and lower on days 1 to 2 (drug F(1,201) = 3.08, P = .08; time F(8,201) = 3.54; drug × time F(8,201) = 4.68, both P < .001). Peak BPRS positive change during ketamine averaged +3.1 points (SD 3.4), from −2 to +9.
key_findings.locator: Results › Efficacy, 7th paragraph; Table, column Peak Change in BPRS Positive Symptoms Subscale Score

key_findings.finding: A trend for an inverse relationship between day-1 percentage change in HDRS and the peak change in BPRS positive score (r = −0.46, P = .06): larger psychotic-type rises went with larger improvement; no other characteristic in the Table predicted response.
key_findings.note: Editors' calculation from the Table's 17 pairs (BPRS change in points): r = −0.43, P = .09; the text calls the predictor a peak percentage change, and the Comment calls it the change to 110 minutes (see reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: Adverse effects more common after ketamine than saline: perceptual disturbances, confusion, raised blood pressure, euphoria, dizziness and increased libido; more common after saline: gastrointestinal distress, thirst, headache, metallic taste and constipation. Most ceased within 80 minutes; euphoria and derealization or depersonalization never lasted beyond 110 minutes; no serious adverse events. No counts are given.
The study was planned for 22 patients and stopped at 18 because an interim analysis indicated a very large effect even if the remaining data showed no response.

Blood levels of ketamine and its metabolites were not collected; the authors say differences in drug metabolism cannot be ruled out as a contributor. They cite half-lives of about 2 hours for ketamine and 5 hours for norketamine from other studies.

Registration: NCT00088699, first submitted 30 July 2004; earliest archived version (23 June 2005) has no primary outcome; HDRS reduction between groups entered as primary outcome on 19 June 2006; current record (umbrella protocol, 67 enrolled, 2004 to 2017) lists the MADRS at baseline and day 1; registry entry criterion MADRS of 22 or more.
key_findings.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00088699: Study Details (current record) and Record History, versions 1 (2005-06-23) and 2 (2006-06-19)
key_findings.note: Read from the registry, not from the article; the article prints only the registration number.

reporting_issues.issue: The Figure 2 legend gives n = 18 for HDRS, BPRS and YMRS values that it says come from the completer analysis, but only 13 people received both infusions (17 ketamine and 14 saline infusions, with 4 people missing saline and 1 missing ketamine).
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (Figure 2 legend; Results › Patients, 1st paragraph; Table)
reporting_issues.consequence: The figure's sample size is overstated; the completer estimates, including d = 1.46 and 0.68, rest on 13 people.

reporting_issues.issue: In the first-period analysis the drug × time interaction is printed as F(1,126) = 4.66 with P < .001; with 1 and 126 degrees of freedom that F gives P = .03, while with 8 and 126 (as for time) it gives P < .001 (editors' calculation). The carryover test is printed as F15 = 11.80, P = .004, with the degrees of freedom run together (F(1,15) gives P = .004).
reporting_issues.consequence: Typographical; the printed P values are consistent with 8 and 126, and with 1 and 15, degrees of freedom.

reporting_issues.issue: The predictor of response is described three ways: the peak percentage change in BPRS positive score (Results), the peak change in points (Table column) and the change from baseline to 110 minutes (Comment, 7th paragraph). From the Table's points the correlation with day-1 HDRS change is r = −0.43 (P = .09), not the printed −0.46 (P = .06) (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML (Results › Efficacy, 8th paragraph; Table; Comment, 7th paragraph)
reporting_issues.consequence: Which BPRS measure was correlated cannot be determined; either way the association is a non-significant trend in 17 people and is not evidence that response is independent of psychotomimetic effects.

reporting_issues.issue: The Table's bottom row gives 6.6 (SD 4.7) previous episodes; the 18 rows give 6.67 (SD 4.58) (editors' calculation), and the text calls the same figure lifetime episodes of depression.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; one table value or the summary row may be misprinted.

reporting_issues.issue: The registered eligibility (MADRS of at least 22 at screening and before phase I, with exclusion of anyone whose MADRS fell by more than 25% between the two) differs from the article's (HDRS of 18 or more), and the registered primary outcome was added after the trial ended.
reporting_issues.page: registry record (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00088699, versions 1 and 2) and publisher HTML (Methods › Patient selection, 1st paragraph)
reporting_issues.consequence: The primary outcome cannot be confirmed as pre-specified; the registry record covers several substudies and does not document this trial's analysis plan.

reporting_issues.issue: Adverse effects are listed by name only, with no counts, denominators or method of collection.
reporting_issues.consequence: The trial cannot be used to estimate how often any adverse effect occurs after this infusion.

verification.source_read: publisher full text (HTML), Archives of General Psychiatry 2006;63(8):856-864, at JAMA Network (https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.63.8.856): abstract, all sections, the Table rendered as text, figure legends, author affiliations, article information (correspondence, dates, author contributions, funding/support, acknowledgment) and references; Figures 1 to 3 are images and their values were not extracted; the article has no supplement; no correction notice is linked on the page. Registration and outcome history additionally read from ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00088699 (current record and history versions 1 and 2).
